title: F11 Econ → Tech → Army → Strike — Full Ground Arc

raw.realWorldMeaning: Full operational sequencing: an offensive campaign needs an economic base capable of sustaining production, a tech chain capable of producing the force, the force itself, and the strike. Skipping any phase (over-econ without production, over-tech without units, under-econ without expansion) collapses the campaign before the deadline. This is the integration test for the entire RTS verb set inside one episode.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: End-to-end mission planning under a deadline: build supply pipeline (econ), commission specialised platforms (tech), mass the fleet (army), execute the objective (strike). Each phase has prerequisites and a tick budget; phase imbalance fails the mission.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: full RTS operational arc, phase-budget allocation under deadline, end-to-end mission planning
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Full operational sequencing: an offensive campaign needs an economic base capable of sustaining production, a tech chain capable of producing the force, the force itself, and the strike. Skipping any phase (over-econ without production, over-tech without units, under-econ without expansion) collapses the campaign before the deadline. This is the integration test for the entire RTS verb set inside one episode.
summary.zh: 完整的作战顺序：进攻性战役需要能够维持生产的经济基础、能够产生力量、力量本身和打击的技术链。跳过任何阶段（经济过度而没有生产、技术过度而没有单位、经济不足而没有扩张）都会导致竞选活动在截止日期前崩溃。这是对一集中的整个 RTS 动词集的集成测试。

en:
Commander, this is the full operational arc — econ to fund, tech to enable, army to mass, strike to win. Your western base at (8,20) holds a Construction Yard, a Power Plant, an Ore Refinery and a single Harvester. Two ore patches sit just east of the refinery. Cash on hand: $5500. The enemy holds a base at (82,20), 74 cells east, with a single rifleman picket. A light tank raid arrives around tick 1500 and a rifleman push around tick 3000. Build a War Factory AND a Service Depot, field at least four medium tanks, then raze at least one enemy production building — all within about 100 turns. Keep your Construction Yard standing.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'weap' → THEN → own a 'fix' → THEN → have ≥4 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy ≥1 enemy buildings AND before game tick 8900 AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 8901 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 100 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, this is the full operational arc against a defended enemy base with mid-game pressure. Your western base at (8,20) holds a Construction Yard, two Power Plants, an Ore Refinery and two starter Harvesters. Three ore patches sit east of the refinery. Cash on hand: $8000. The enemy holds a defended base at (98,20), 90 cells east, with riflemen and a rocket soldier. A mid-game tank raid arrives around tick 1500 and a main attack around tick 3000. Build a War Factory AND a Service Depot, field at least five medium tanks, then raze at least two enemy buildings — all within about 105 turns. Keep your Construction Yard standing.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'weap' → THEN → own a 'fix' → THEN → have ≥5 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy ≥2 enemy buildings AND before game tick 9300 AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 9301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 105 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, this is the full operational arc against a defended enemy under continuous waves. Your western base spawns NORTH (y=12) or SOUTH (y=28) by seed — read your actual starting band from the observation. Each spawn holds a Construction Yard, two Power Plants, an Ore Refinery and two starter Harvesters. Three ore patches sit adjacent. Cash on hand: $9500. The enemy holds a defended base at (98,20), with riflemen, rocket soldiers, a pre-positioned medium tank, and two timed waves — a hunt-tank raid around tick 1500 and a main attack around tick 3000. Build a War Factory AND a Service Depot, field at least six medium tanks, then raze at least three enemy buildings — all within about 150 turns. Keep your Construction Yard standing.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'weap' → THEN → own a 'fix' → THEN → have ≥6 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy buildings AND before game tick 13000 AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 13001 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 150 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.
zh:
指挥官，这就是完整的作战弧线——经济到资金、技术到启用、军队到集结、打击到胜利。你位于（8,20）的西部基地拥有一个建筑场、一个发电厂、一个矿石精炼厂和一个收割机。炼油厂东边有两个矿区。库存现金：5500 美元。敌方在东边 74 号牢房（82,20）拥有一个基地，只有一名步枪兵哨兵。一场轻型坦克突袭在 1500 点左右到达，一名步枪手在 3000 点左右推进。建造一座战争工厂和一个服务站，部署至少四辆中型坦克，然后夷平至少一栋敌方生产建筑 - 所有这些都在大约 100 回合内完成。保持您的施工场地站立。
胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：拥有一个“武器”→然后→拥有一个“修复”→然后→拥有≥4个“2tnk”→然后→摧毁≥1个敌方建筑物并且在游戏刻8900之前并拥有≥1个“事实”建筑物。

title: F11 Full Combined Arms — Ground + Air + Naval

raw.realWorldMeaning: Three-domain combined-arms doctrine: a campaign-scale strike package requires ALL THREE arms — ground (medium tanks for overland push and armoured firepower), air (helicopters for terrain-ignoring rapid engagement of midfield targets), and naval (destroyers for coastal shore-strike standoff range across a water barrier). Targets are distributed across three reachability domains so no single arm can hit the whole kill quota; the cash + tick budget must be split across three parallel production streams.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Tri-modal robot fleet operation: a coastal + interior survey or interdiction mission may require surface vehicles (overland, high-payload), aerial drones (terrain-ignoring, fast), and surface ships (water domain, long standoff range). Each modality is essential to its domain; missing any modality fails objectives in that domain.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: tri-domain combined-arms doctrine, ground + air + naval campaign, tri-modal robot fleet composition
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.zh: 三域联合兵种学说：战役规模的打击一揽子计划需要所有三种兵种——地面（用于陆上推进和装甲火力的中型坦克）、空中（用于无视地形快速攻击中场目标的直升机）和海军（用于跨越水障的沿海海岸打击防区外范围的驱逐舰）。目标分布在三个可达域中，因此没有一个手臂可以达到整个杀戮配额；现金+蜱预算必须分配给三个并行的生产流。

title: F11 Pivot on Scout — Reactive Arm-Picking

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reactive perception loop: an opposing force commits to a particular composition; the commander observes it, picks the counter (the RPS choice — armour beats massed infantry; air beats armour without anti-air), and produces the counter under a clock. The hardest version is when the opposing force pivots mid-engagement — the commander must re-observe and re-pivot rather than executing a one-shot plan.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Closed-loop adversarial scenario planning: a robot mission where the target set is dynamic (a search-and-engage task where the target type changes between sorties). A robot that chooses its tooling once at sortie-start and never re-observes fails when the target set changes mid-mission.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: rock-paper-scissors counter-pick under perception, AlphaStar / SC2 reactive build-order pivot, OODA-loop re-observation
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.zh: 反应性感知循环：相反的力量致力于特定的构图；指挥官观察它，选择计数器（RPS选择——装甲击败密集的步兵；空中击败没有防空的装甲），并在时钟下产生计数器。最困难的版本是当敌方部队在交战中转向时——指挥官必须重新观察和重新转向，而不是执行一次性计划。

title: F11 Rebuild After Attrition — Disaster Recovery

raw.realWorldMeaning: Disaster recovery / industrial-accident replanning: the commander has an established production base and an offensive objective; mid-episode an exogenous strike (sabotage, industrial accident, supply-line cut) destroys part of the production line. The commander must rebuild the lost capability, restart production, and still finish the offensive on the ORIGINAL deadline — no extension. The PlanBench replanning idiom: the plan that worked at t=0 is invalidated at t=mid, and the repair plus the original goal must both fit inside the unchanged budget.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Mission resilience under a component-failure / station-loss event: a multi-robot warehouse where a charging station goes offline mid-shift; the system must redirect, recharge from secondary capacity, and still hit the day's throughput.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning under exogenous failure, SC2 comeback (rebuild after bad trade, keep timing), SRE disaster recovery / industrial-accident response
raw.author: openra-bench

title: F11 Vertical Strike — Ground + Air Combined Arms

raw.realWorldMeaning: Combined-arms doctrine: a vertical-envelopment strike package requires BOTH a ground manoeuvre arm (medium tanks for armoured push and absorbing direct fire) AND an air arm (helicopters for over-terrain mobility and rapid target engagement). A pure-ground force is slow over open distance and cannot bypass enemy defensive geometry; a pure-air force is shredded by anti-air emplacements without a ground escort to suppress them. The capability under test is allocating cash and tick budget across two production streams in parallel — a war factory AND a helipad — and producing the minimum vertical force composition before the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Heterogeneous fleet composition: a delivery / mapping mission may require both surface robots (high-payload, slow, terrain-bound) and aerial drones (low-payload, fast, terrain-ignoring) to clear a mixed-objective task by deadline. Sending only one modality fails on the objectives the OTHER modality is suited for.

raw.author: openra-bench

A pure-ground force cannot economically range coastal positions defended by infantry on the shore; a pure-naval force cannot project power past the immediate shoreline. The capability under test is allocating cash, build time, and the spatial placement of a SHIPYARD (which must sit adjacent to a water cell to function) across two production streams in parallel.
summary.zh: 跨两个物理领域（陆地+水域）的联合兵种条令：沿海打击一揽子计划既需要地面机动兵力（中型坦克推动驱逐舰无法到达的内陆轴线），又需要海军兵力（驱逐舰从海岸线的防区外范围炮击沿海目标）。纯地面部队无法在经济上对由岸上步兵保卫的沿海阵地进行射程；纯粹的海军力量无法将兵力投送至海岸线以外。所测试的功能是在两个生产流中并行分配现金、建造时间和造船厂的空间布局（必须毗邻水池才能发挥作用）。

en:
Commander, this is a coastal vertical strike. You must build BOTH a War Factory AND a Shipyard, field at least two medium tanks AND at least one destroyer (a naval warship that floats on water and cannot move onto land), then raze at least two enemy buildings — one coastal AND one deep inland — all within about 100 turns. Your western base at (8,20) sits west of a vertical water channel running from x=22 to x=24. Cash on hand: $6000. The enemy holds a coastal Barracks at (27,8) just east of the shoreline (a destroyer's naval gun reaches it from the channel) AND a deep inland Construction Yard at (95,20), far past any naval range. A Shipyard MUST be built ADJACENT to a water cell to function — placing one at (20,20) puts its east edge on the shoreline. Ground units can pass around the water through the open corridors at y<8 (north) and y>33 (south). Keep your western Construction Yard standing.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'weap' → THEN → own a 'syrd' → THEN → have ≥2 '2tnk' AND have ≥1 'dd' → THEN → destroy ≥2 enemy buildings AND before game tick 8900 AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 8901 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 100 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, this is a coastal vertical strike against a heavier garrison with a mid-game overland tank raid. You must build BOTH a War Factory AND a Shipyard, field at least three medium tanks AND at least one destroyer, then raze at least three enemy buildings (with at least one coastal AND one inland) — all within about 110 turns. Your western base at (8,20) sits west of a vertical water channel from x=22 to x=24 with two starter Harvesters. Cash on hand: $8500. The enemy holds two coastal buildings (Barracks and Power Plant) just east of the shoreline (in destroyer range) AND a deep inland base at (95,20) past any naval reach. A tank rush of 2 medium tanks arrives from the inland axis around tick 3000. A Shipyard MUST be built ADJACENT to a water cell.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'weap' → THEN → own a 'syrd' → THEN → have ≥3 '2tnk' AND have ≥1 'dd' → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy buildings AND before game tick 9800 AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 9801 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 110 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, this is a coastal vertical strike against a defended enemy base under timed waves. Your western base spawns NORTH (y=12) or SOUTH (y=28) by seed and sits west of a 3-cell water channel from x=22 to x=24. The enemy holds three coastal positions (Barracks, Power Plant, and a defense Turret that fires on naval targets in range), two deep-inland buildings past naval reach, and lands two timed waves — an overland tank rusher around tick 4500 and a rocket- soldier reinforcement around tick 6500. YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 14001 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 160 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

失败条件：（不在游戏刻 14001 之前或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物）或你的整个部队被摧毁）。

title: Harass Response — Engage the Probe, Don't Bleed the Defence

raw.realWorldMeaning: A perimeter alert appears inside live infrastructure (a small probing patrol oscillates onto your refinery). You must pick contain / monitor / hunt without bleeding capacity to the distractor. The intended policy keeps the fire team ON the asset and ORDERS them to engage as the probe swings into range — fire support on home turf. Doing nothing (monitor) lets the probe chip the asset to death; chasing the probe off-map (hunt) overextends the team into the next alt-vector swing and abandons the asset; pulling back (yield / retreat) also abandons the asset. The discrimination is between "respond proportionally on home turf" and three failure modes that all bleed something (the asset, the team, or both).
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Security robot reacting to a probe without leaving the patrol zone unmanned: engage the intruder within the asset's defended footprint; do not pursue past the leash or the parallel sector goes uncovered.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: τ²-bench distractor handling, MineRL react vs pursue wildlife, SOC Tier-2 triage: contain vs monitor vs hunt, perimeter alert response under preservation constraint
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.zh: 实时基础设施内会出现周边警报（小型探测巡逻队会进入您的炼油厂）。你必须选择遏制/监视/狩猎，而不会对干扰者造成流血能力。预期的政策是让火力小组留在资产上，并命令他们在探测器进入射程时进行交战——在主场进行火力支援。如果不采取任何措施（监控），探测器就会将资产毁掉；在地图外追逐探测器（狩猎）会使团队过度延伸到下一个替代向量摆动并放弃资产；撤回（屈服/撤退）也会放弃该资产。区别在于“在自己的地盘上按比例做出反应”和三种都会造成某些损失（资产、团队或两者）的失败模式。

en:
Commander, this is a base-defence response. You are given an Ore Refinery at (16,20) and a 5-man rifle-infantry garrison clustered around it at (13-14, 18-22), all on hold-fire orders — they will not engage unless you order them to. A single enemy rifleman patrols inside the perimeter on a patrol script, oscillating between (14,20) and (30,20). Score 1 kill, keep the Refinery intact, keep at least 4 garrison alive, lose no more than 2, within 4500 ticks.
WIN WHEN: destroy ≥1 enemy units AND keep ≥4 units alive AND lose ≤2 of your own units AND own a 'proc' AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR NOT (lose ≤2 of your own units) OR NOT (own a 'proc')).
You have at most 55 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, this is a base-defence response. You are given an Ore Refinery at (16,20) and a 5-man rifle-infantry garrison clustered around it at (13-14, 18-22), all on hold-fire orders. title: 100-Turn Marathon Survival — Sustain Defence, Reinforcement, and Repair

raw.realWorldMeaning: A very-late single-episode endurance test: keep the base alive under SUSTAINED enemy pressure for the full 100-turn budget. The win is gated on the base, a minimum garrison, and the pillbox line ALL still being intact at the end of the run, not on a one-shot decision. The intended capability is the cadence of reinforcement (train new infantry every few turns), repair (toggle autorepair on damaged defences), and economic stewardship (keep the refinery's harvester flowing). Stalling, pure defence without reinforcement, and pure construction without repair all lose; only sustained operations survive to the after-ticks gate.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Long-horizon autonomous operation under continuous external pressure: an extended on-call / extended deployment where there is no single decisive action, only the discipline of sustained maintenance — repair work, supply replenishment, force rotation — across the entire window. Credit only arrives at the end of the window if every subsystem is still up.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: lmgame-Bench multi-hour endurance, SC2LE full-game / extended-game testing, long-horizon credit assignment, SRE extended on-call / military endurance ops
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: A very-late single-episode endurance test: keep the base alive under SUSTAINED enemy pressure for the full 100-turn budget. The win is gated on the base, a minimum garrison, and the pillbox line ALL still being intact at the end of the run, not on a one-shot decision. The intended capability is the cadence of reinforcement (train new infantry every few turns), repair (toggle autorepair on damaged defences), and economic stewardship (keep the refinery's harvester flowing). Stalling, pure defence without reinforcement, and pure construction without repair all lose; only sustained operations survive to the after-ticks gate.
summary.zh: 非常晚的单集耐力测试：在完整的 100 回合预算中，在敌人持续的压力下保持基地的生存。胜利取决于基地、最少的驻军以及在冲刺结束时所有碉堡线仍然完好无损，而不是一击决定。预期的能力是加强的节奏（每隔几个回合训练新的步兵）、修复（在受损的防御系统上切换自动修复）和经济管理（保持炼油厂的收割机运转）。拖延、纯防御不加固、纯建设不修复都输了；只有持续的操作才能存活到后刻度门。

title: Build Army → Coordinate Multi-Front Attack — Mass-Then-Split

raw.realWorldMeaning: Late-game two-phase operational plan: first ASSEMBLE a real fighting force (≥N medium tanks built from the pre-placed war factory), then COMMIT that force to a simultaneous TWO-FRONT assault on two separated enemy headquarters (NE and SE corners). The `then:` composite enforces the assemble-before-attack ordering and the 120-cell NE↔SE separation enforces the SPLIT — a single mass cannot raze both corners in sequence inside the clock; only build-then-split wins. Sending only the 2 starter units to each front fails (insufficient firepower per prong); stalling fails on the clock; one-front-only fails on the second destruction clause.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Theater-wide operational sequencing: a force must be brought to minimum operational strength BEFORE being committed, and once committed must be split across two simultaneous objectives in different theatres under a single shared deadline. A serialized "clear theatre A then redeploy to B" plan blows the time budget; a "commit understrength to both" plan loses both engagements.

title: Credit Only at the Final Phase — Sparse Reward, One Late Objective

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long-horizon plan where ONLY the terminal outcome is rewarded: raze the far enemy headquarters inside a single late deadline. Building the base, massing the army, marching across the map — none of it scores on its own. The agent must invest early with no feedback, then commit the force on a long trek so the one rewarded event lands in time. Over-investing (building forever, never striking) and under-investing (striking too early with too little) both lose; only correctly-timed commitment toward the distant payoff wins. This is delayed gratification under sparse reward.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: A multi-stage autonomous mission where success is graded solely on completing the final objective by a hard deadline (e.g. a long traverse-then-deliver task): intermediate waypoints and subsystem readiness earn no partial credit, so the planner must allocate the whole time budget toward the single terminal payoff rather than optimising locally-visible sub-progress.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: sparse-reward RL (terminal-only reward, no reward shaping), delayed-gratification / temporal credit assignment, long-horizon credit assignment (terminal-objective payoff), Montezuma's Revenge-style sparse terminal reward
raw.author: berta

summary.en: A long-horizon plan where ONLY the terminal outcome is rewarded: raze the far enemy headquarters inside a single late deadline. Over-investing (building forever, never striking) and under-investing (striking too early with too little) both lose; only correctly-timed commitment toward the distant payoff wins. This is delayed gratification under sparse reward.
summary.zh: 这是一个只奖励最终结果的长远计划：在一个较晚的期限内夷平远处的敌人总部。建造基地、集结军队、在地图上行军——这些都不是靠自己就能得分的。代理人必须在没有反馈的情况下尽早投入，然后投入长途跋涉的力量，以便奖励活动及时落地。过度投资（永远建设，从不罢工）和投资不足（过早罢工，投入太少）都会失败；只有对遥远的回报做出正确的承诺才能获胜。这是稀疏奖励下的延迟满足。

title: Secure → Tech → Second Base — 3-Phase Long-Horizon Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode macro plan whose final win depends on each intermediate phase being observed-true in order: harden the home base with static defences (pillboxes) under live patrol pressure, unlock the tech tree (war factory), then commit the spare MCV eastward to stand up a second Construction Yard inside the briefed expansion region. The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces strict happened-before — a policy that expands before tech, or teches before defences, cannot satisfy the chain.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-site ramp-up of a long-horizon mission with strict stage gating: harden the home site against active adversarial pressure, bring the upgraded production capability online, then deploy a base-builder platform to the designated expansion sector and convert it into a second operational site — all within one budget. Out-of-order completion (expand before hardening, or expand before the upgraded capability is online) forfeits the chain.

title: Econ → Army → Victory — Strict 3-Phase Macro Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode macro plan whose final win depends on three sequenced milestones: first accumulate enough economy_value (cash + uncashed resources) via harvest income; then assemble a real fighting force (≥6 own units); then commit them to terminal action (≥K enemy kills). The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces happened-before sequencing — pre-spending all cash on an army before income tops up the M bar cannot complete phase 1, and building economy without ever fielding/attacking with an army cannot complete phases 2-3. Only the intended econ → army → victory chain WINS inside the tick budget.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Long-horizon agentic operation with strict stage gating in an industrial / military context: revenue / fuel / logistics must clear a readiness bar BEFORE a fleet is provisioned, which must be provisioned BEFORE a terminal action (sortie / market entry / mission execution). The credit at episode end requires each stage to have happened, in order, inside one budget window — skipping any stage forfeits the chain.

raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: A long single-episode macro plan whose final win depends on three sequenced milestones: first accumulate enough economy_value (cash + uncashed resources) via harvest income; then assemble a real fighting force (≥6 own units); then commit them to terminal action (≥K enemy kills). The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces happened-before sequencing — pre-spending all cash on an army before income tops up the M bar cannot complete phase 1, and building economy without ever fielding/attacking with an army cannot complete phases 2-3. Only the intended econ → army → victory chain WINS inside the tick budget.
summary.zh: 一个漫长的单集宏观计划，其最终胜利取决于三个有序的里程碑：首先通过收获收入积累足够的经济价值（现金+未兑现的资源）；然后组建一支真正的战斗部队（≥6个自己的部队）；然后让他们进行最终行动（杀死≥K个敌人）。 Wave-2“然后：”复合强制执行先发生后排序——在收入达到 M 条之前将所有现金预先花在军队上无法完成第 1 阶段，而在没有部署/攻击军队的情况下建设经济也无法完成第 2-3 阶段。只有预期的经济→军队→胜利链才能在预算范围内获胜。

en:
Commander, you have a western base — Construction Yard, ore refinery, power plant, barracks and one harvester — feeding a near ore patch at about 95 credits per turn. No starting army. Two enemy riflemen on hold-fire wait mid-map (they will NOT shoot, even if attacked); a persistent enemy yard sits in the far east. Win bar: economy value at least 1500, at least six own units, and at least two unit kills, within about 50 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: reach economy value ≥1500 (cash+ore) → THEN → keep ≥6 units alive → THEN → destroy ≥2 enemy units AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 50 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, your western base — Construction Yard, ore refinery, power plant, barracks and one harvester on a near patch (~95 credits/turn) — has no starting army. Three enemy riflemen on hold-fire wait mid-map; a persistent enemy yard sits far east. Win bar: economy value at least 2200, at least six own units, and at least three unit kills, within about 50 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: reach economy value ≥2200 (cash+ore) → THEN → keep ≥6 units alive → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy units AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 50 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, your western base — Construction Yard, ore refinery, power plant, barracks and one harvester — spawns NORTH (y=14) or SOUTH (y=22) by seed; the spawn-matched ore patch flips with it. Four enemy riflemen on hold-fire wait mid-map; a persistent enemy yard sits far east. Win bar: economy value at least 2500, at least six own units, and at least three unit kills, within about 60 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) → THEN → keep ≥6 units alive → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy units AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.
zh:
指挥官，您有一个西部基地 - 建筑场、矿石精炼厂、发电厂、营房和一台收割机 - 以每回合约 95 个信用点为附近的矿区提供饲料。无始发军。两名敌方步枪手在地图中央等待（即使受到攻击，他们也不会射击）；远东有一个顽固的敌人庭院。胜利条：经济值至少1500，至少6个己方单位，至少2个单位杀戮，大约50回合内。

失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 4501 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 50 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：达到经济价值≥2200（现金+矿石）→然后→保持≥6个单位存活→然后→消灭≥3个敌方单位并在游戏刻4500之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 4501 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 50 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

指挥官，您的西部基地 - 建筑场、矿石精炼厂、发电厂、营房和一台收割机 - 通过种子生成北方 (y=14) 或南方 (y=22)；与之匹配的矿石块也会随之翻转。四名敌方步枪手在地图中央等待；远东有一个顽固的敌人院子。胜利条：经济值至少2500，至少6个己方单位，至少击杀3个单位，大约60回合内。
胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：达到经济价值≥2500（现金+矿石）→然后→保持≥6个单位存活→然后→摧毁≥3个敌方单位并在游戏刻5400之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 5401 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 60 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

title: Multi-Checkpoint 5+ — Strict Long-Sequencing Chain (PERT / PlanBench)

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode operation whose final win depends on FIVE or more intermediate checkpoints being observed-true in order: stand up the economy (refinery), unlock the tech (war factory), produce a real fighting force (≥2 medium tanks), engage and accumulate kills (≥3), then commit to the terminal objective (raze the enemy headquarters). The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces strict happened-before — an out-of-order completion (kills before the army, attack before the tech) cannot advance the chain past the skipped clause and forfeits the episode on the clock.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Long sequenced operation with strict checkpoint gating: a mission that runs through 5+ phases that must complete in order (sensor coverage → infrastructure → fleet provisioning → contact → objective), inside a single budget window. Credit at episode end requires every phase to have happened in sequence — out-of-order completion forfeits the whole chain. Standard PERT / CPM critical-path execution where a downstream task cannot start (and cannot earn credit) until its upstream predecessor has finished.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench long-sequencing, PERT critical path, PERT/CPM project management, long SOP execution
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: A long single-episode operation whose final win depends on FIVE or more intermediate checkpoints being observed-true in order: stand up the economy (refinery), unlock the tech (war factory), produce a real fighting force (≥2 medium tanks), engage and accumulate kills (≥3), then commit to the terminal objective (raze the enemy headquarters). The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces strict happened-before — an out-of-order completion (kills before the army, attack before the tech) cannot advance the chain past the skipped clause and forfeits the episode on the clock.
summary.zh: 一场漫长的单集行动，其最终胜利取决于观察到的五个或更多中间检查站 - 按顺序排列：发展经济（炼油厂），解锁科技（战争工厂），生产真正的战斗力量（≥2中型坦克），交战并积累杀戮（≥3），然后致力于最终目标（夷平敌人总部）。 Wave-2“then:”组合强制执行严格的“发生前事件”——无序完成（在军队之前杀戮，在技术之前攻击）无法将链推进到跳过的子句并放弃时钟上的情节。

en:
Commander, you have a western base — Construction Yard, barracks, power plant, service depot, four medium tanks on Defend stance — at (10,18). An undefended enemy headquarters sits at (80,30); a sentinel enemy yard sits north. Win bar: own a refinery, own a war factory, and raze the enemy yard, within about 85 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'proc' → THEN → own a 'weap' → THEN → destroy the enemy fact AND before game tick 7200.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 7201 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 85 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, your western base at (10,18) — Construction Yard, barracks, power, service depot, four medium tanks on Defend — faces an enemy headquarters at (80,30) defended by three rifles and one rocket soldier on hold-fire (they will NOT shoot back). Win bar: own a refinery, own a war factory, field at least two medium tanks, accumulate at least three kills, and raze the enemy yard, within about 85 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'proc' → THEN → own a 'weap' → THEN → have ≥2 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy units → THEN → destroy the enemy fact AND before game tick 7200.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 7201 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 85 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Commander, your western base — Construction Yard, barracks, power, service depot, four medium tanks on Defend — spawns NORTH (y=14) or SOUTH (y=26) by seed. The enemy headquarters at (80,20) is defended by three rifles and two rocket soldiers on hold-fire. Win bar: own a refinery, own a war factory, field at least two medium tanks, accumulate at least three kills, field at least four medium tanks, and raze the enemy yard, within about 85 turns.
WIN WHEN: in this exact order: own a 'proc' → THEN → own a 'weap' → THEN → have ≥2 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy ≥3 enemy units → THEN → have ≥4 '2tnk' → THEN → destroy the enemy fact AND before game tick 7200.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 7201 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 85 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.
zh:
指挥官，您有一个西部基地——建筑工场、营房、发电厂、服务站、四辆处于防御姿态的中型坦克——位于（10,18）。不设防的敌军总部位于 (80,30)；敌方哨兵院子位于北面。胜利吧：拥有一个炼油厂，拥有一个战争工厂，并在大约85回合内夷平敌人的庭院。
胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：拥有一个“过程”→然后→拥有一个“武器”→然后→摧毁敌人的事实并且在游戏7200之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 7201 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 85 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

指挥官，您位于 (10,18) 的西部基地——建筑工场、营房、电力、服务站、防御上的四辆中型坦克——面对位于 (80,30) 的敌方总部，该总部由三支步枪和一名处于停火状态的火箭兵防守（他们不会还击）。胜利条：拥有炼油厂，拥有战争工厂，部署至少两辆中型坦克，积累至少三场杀戮，并在大约85回合内夷平敌人的庭院。
胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：拥有一个“proc”→然后→拥有一个“武器”→然后→拥有≥2个“2tnk”→然后→摧毁≥3个敌方单位→然后→摧毁敌方事实并在游戏刻7200之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 7201 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 85 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

指挥官，您的西部基地 - 建筑场、兵营、电力、服务站、防御上的四辆中型坦克 - 通过种子生成北方 (y=14) 或南方 (y=26)。 (80,20)处的敌军总部由三支步枪和两名火箭兵守卫，并保持射击状态。胜利条：拥有一座炼油厂，拥有一座战争工厂，部署至少两辆中型坦克，累积至少三场击杀，部署至少四辆中型坦克，并在约85回合内夷平敌方庭院。
胜利条件：按照这个确切的顺序：拥有一个“proc”→然后→拥有一个“weap”→然后→拥有≥2个“2tnk”→然后→摧毁≥3个敌方单位→然后→拥有≥4个“2tnk”→然后→摧毁敌方事实并在游戏刻7200之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 7201 或不（拥有 ≥1 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 85 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

title: Opening → Defense → Counter — Strict 3-Phase Military Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode military plan whose final win depends on three sequenced milestones: first bring the base online (build the power plant so the pre-placed barracks/refinery come online); then survive a concentrated opening rush (kill enough of the rushers and hold the line past a defence window); then convert the survived defence into an offensive that destroys the enemy construction yard far to the east. The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces happened-before sequencing — stalling loses the base to the rush, racing the counter first loses the base while undefended, and a pure defence that never counter-attacks cannot complete the chain. Only the intended opening → defense → counter plan WINS inside the tick budget.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Long-horizon agentic operation with strict stage gating in a military / incident-response context: a site must first be brought to operational readiness (power online so the line can run), then survive a concentrated incoming attack (contain the spike and hold past the incident window), then mount the planned response that neutralises the source of the attack. Each stage gates the next inside one budget window — skipping any stage (no readiness, no defence, no response) forfeits the chain.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 timing push, military defense-then-counter, PlanBench long-sequencing, incident response: stabilise then remediate the source
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Opening → Tech → Army → Engage — Strict 4-Phase Macro Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode macro plan whose final win depends on each intermediate phase being observed-true in order: stand up the economy (refinery), unlock the tech (war factory), build a real fighting force (≥4 medium tanks), then commit them to a positional objective (the enemy headquarters). The Wave-2 `then:` composite enforces strict happened-before — a policy that pre-builds units before the tech, or attacks before the army is assembled, cannot satisfy the chain.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Long-horizon agentic operation with strict stage gating: a mission must complete each phase in order (sensor coverage, infrastructure, fleet provisioning, terminal action) within one budget window; credit at episode end requires each stage to have happened in sequence — out-of-order completion forfeits the chain.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE full-game macro chain, lmgame-Bench multi-hour long-horizon, PlanBench multi-stage credit assignment, product roadmap: foundation → R&D → ship → market
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Stage-Locked Progression — PERT Critical-Path 5-Stage Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: A long single-episode operation whose final win depends on FIVE milestones being observed-true in strict order: bring power online (power plant), stand up resource intake (ore refinery), accumulate a capital reserve (economy_value ≥ M), unlock the tech tier (war factory), then commit to terminal action (≥ K kills). The Wave-2 `then:` composite is a PERT critical path — each milestone node gates its successor, so skipping a stage is impossible by construction: the latch cannot advance past a stage that was never observed true, and the chain never completes. Only the intended ordered progression wins inside the tick budget; any stage-skip or stall forfeits on the clock.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: PERT/CPM critical-path execution of a staged operation: a mission runs through power-up, resource intake, capital/charge reserve, capability unlock and terminal action, and the credit at episode end requires every stage to have happened in sequence inside one budget window. A downstream task cannot start — and cannot earn credit — until its upstream predecessor has finished; an out-of-order or skipped stage forfeits the whole staged plan.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PERT critical path, PlanBench staged dependencies, project management, PERT/CPM project management, PlanBench long-sequencing

title: Disaster Recovery — Rebuild After a Mid-Game Loss, Still Finish

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reactive replan after a mid-mission exogenous catastrophe wipes part of the operating force and the economy at once. An offensive operation runs on a fixed deadline with a working production base (Construction Yard + Refinery + Power Plant + War Factory + Ore Truck + ore patch) and a forward armoured column. Mid-episode a scheduled disaster — a sabotage strike, a supply-line cut, an industrial accident — destroys the Ore Refinery and two of the forward tanks. The deadline does not move. The model must notice the loss (the live refinery count drops to zero, the tank count falls), commit the reserve to rebuilding the refinery so the income channel is restored, AND press on with the surviving and replacement force to clear the eastern garrison before the original clock expires. Giving up after the loss, rebuilding but never attacking, or attacking but never rebuilding the refinery all miss the bar.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Disaster recovery / PlanBench replanning under an exogenous failure event. An autonomous operation loses a critical infrastructure node and part of its mobile fleet to a single mid-mission catastrophe; the operational objective and timeline are unchanged. Recovery requires recognising the compound loss, committing the reserve to rebuilding the lost infrastructure (not to more mobile units, not to nothing), and continuing the mission with the regenerated force fast enough that the original deadline is still met — the SC2 comeback: rebuild after a bad trade and still hit the timing.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning, disaster recovery, SC2 comeback
raw.author: openra-bench-wave-11

summary.en: Reactive replan after a mid-mission exogenous catastrophe wipes part of the operating force and the economy at once. An offensive operation runs on a fixed deadline with a working production base (Construction Yard + Refinery + Power Plant + War Factory + Ore Truck + ore patch) and a forward armoured column. Mid-episode a scheduled disaster — a sabotage strike, a supply-line cut, an industrial accident — destroys the Ore Refinery and two of the forward tanks. The deadline does not move. The model must notice the loss (the live refinery count drops to zero, the tank count falls), commit the reserve to rebuilding the refinery so the income channel is restored, AND press on with the surviving and replacement force to clear the eastern garrison before the original clock expires. Giving up after the loss, rebuilding but never attacking, or attacking but never rebuilding the refinery all miss the bar.
summary.zh: 任务中期外生灾难后的反应性重新计划立即消灭了部分作战部队和经济。进攻行动在固定期限内进行，有一个工作生产基地（建筑场+炼油厂+发电厂+战争工厂+矿石卡车+矿石场）和前方装甲纵队。剧情中期，一场预定的灾难——破坏性罢工、供应线切断、工业事故——摧毁了矿石精炼厂和两辆前方坦克。截止日期不变。该模型必须注意到损失（现有炼油厂数量降至零，坦克数量下降），将储备用于重建炼油厂，以便恢复收入渠道，并在原始时钟到期之前继续与幸存和替代部队一起清除东部驻军。损失后放弃，重建但不进攻，或者进攻但不重建炼油厂，都没有达到标准。

en:
A working base (yard, refinery, power, war factory, harvester) and four heavy-tank raiders heading east to a five-rifle garrison. Around tick 1500 a scripted sabotage wipes the refinery AND two of four tanks. Rebuild the refinery, push on with the survivors, and finish five kills before tick 5400.
WIN WHEN: destroy ≥5 enemy units AND own ≥1 'proc' building(s) AND not before game tick 1600 AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Scout, React, Counter — Observation-Driven 3-Phase Chain

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reactive macro on a fixed force: the agent must drive the observation-action-counter loop end-to-end inside one budget. Phase 1 (scout) is mandatory — the deeper enemy posture (≥2 buildings worth of structure) must be observed before any commit is informed; phase 2 (react) requires the army to actually engage the cluster, not merely walk past; phase 3 (counter) is the production-yard kill that ends the threat at its source. Pre-committing to attack the construction yard without scouting cannot satisfy the chain — the scout latch is the load-bearing first link.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Threat-intel-driven incident response: SOC analyst confirms multiple indicators of compromise from telemetry (scout), contains the active attacker on the network (react / engage), then patches the upstream attack vector / takes down the command-and-control host (counter). Skipping the confirmation step and going straight to take-down acts on stale belief and misses the root cause; scouting forever bleeds the response window.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 reactive macro (scout-pivot-counter), CICERO information-action loop, PlanBench replanning, threat-intel-driven defense
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Reactive macro on a fixed force: the agent must drive the observation-action-counter loop end-to-end inside one budget. Phase 1 (scout) is mandatory — the deeper enemy posture (≥2 buildings worth of structure) must be observed before any commit is informed; phase 2 (react) requires the army to actually engage the cluster, not merely walk past; phase 3 (counter) is the production-yard kill that ends the threat at its source. Pre-committing to attack the construction yard without scouting cannot satisfy the chain — the scout latch is the load-bearing first link.
summary.zh: 固定力上的反应性宏：智能体必须在一个预算内端到端地驱动观察-行动-计数器循环。第 1 阶段（侦察）是强制性的——在通知任何提交之前，必须观察更深的敌人态势（≥2 栋建筑物的结构）；第二阶段（反应）要求军队实际与集群交战，而不仅仅是走过去；第三阶段（反击）是生产场杀戮，从源头结束威胁。在没有侦察的情况下预先承诺攻击施工场地并不能满足链条的需要——侦察闩锁是承重的第一环节。

title: Late Tech-Pivot Attack — Scout, Pivot the Counter, Raze the Base

raw.realWorldMeaning: Late-game three-phase macro: tech is already standing, but the initial assault plan must be revised mid-episode once scouting reveals the actual enemy composition. The pivot does NOT discard the sunk tech costs (the existing barracks + war factory remain the production substrate for either counter), and the final score depends on every phase still being satisfied at the end — scout, pivot to the correct counter, then commit to razing the enemy construction yard inside the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Product pivot from V1 to V2 on market data: the foundational engineering (infra, hiring) is sunk and reusable, but the active build target must switch mid-cycle once scouting (a customer pilot) reveals which feature wins the market. title: Army Over Tech — Commit to Units Under a Fast Rush

raw.realWorldMeaning: A strategic-commitment decision under a hard time constraint: the base infrastructure is already standing, and a fixed budget buys EITHER an immediate fighting force (OPEX — cheap units fielded now) OR a throughput investment (CAPEX — a second war factory, an upgrade) that would pay off later. A fast incoming rush collapses the time horizon: the capex investment cannot amortise before the base is lost, so the only winning play is to commit the whole budget to army NOW. Teching up under the rush — and stalling — both lose the base before the investment returns; the intended army-rush blunts the charge and survives.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Capex-vs-opex under an acute threat: with a live incident bearing down (a DDoS spike, a competitor's fast launch, an incoming assault), a fixed budget buys EITHER capacity that compounds over months (a second production line, a platform rebuild) OR an immediate response (surge staffing, off-the-shelf units). When the threat clock is short the long-horizon investment never pays back — it must be deferred and the budget spent on the response that fields in time.

A fast incoming rush collapses the time horizon: the capex investment cannot amortise before the base is lost, so the only winning play is to commit the whole budget to army NOW. Teching up under the rush — and stalling — both lose the base before the investment returns; the intended army-rush blunts the charge and survives.
summary.zh: 在困难时期约束下的战略承诺决策：基础设施已经建成，固定预算要么购买一支直接战斗部队（OPEX——现在部署的廉价部队），要么购买稍后会得到回报的吞吐量投资（CAPEX——第二个战争工厂，升级）。快速到来的冲击会破坏时间范围：资本支出投资无法在失去基地之前摊销，因此唯一获胜的策略就是立即将全部预算投入军队。在匆忙中技术进步和停滞不前都会在投资回报之前失去基础；预定的军队冲锋削弱了冲锋并得以幸存。

title: Repair Priority Order — Service the Critical Plant Before the Strike

raw.realWorldMeaning: You inherit a quiet production base whose five structures are pre-damaged to varying degrees and you have a maintenance window before a scheduled stress event hits. The damage picture is misleading: the pillbox is the most worn (20%) and the loudest wear indicator, but it is low value, not load-bearing, and sits away from the coming stress. The refinery, war factory, and construction yard are the load-bearing assets and they are the ones the strike targets. The intended decision is preventive-maintenance triage: service the load-bearing plant to spec BEFORE the known stress event and keep the repair organ on it through the event — not the component whose wear gauge is reddest. Repairing the loud low-value decoys first, or stalling, loses the critical plant when the strike lands.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Preventive-maintenance scheduling / pre-incident hardening: a plant or robot fleet has a known upcoming stress event (a peak-load window, a qualification test, a storm) and a finite service window beforehand. The correct policy services the load-bearing subsystems to spec ahead of the event and keeps them monitored through it, rather than chasing whichever wear indicator looks worst. The same criticality-weighted, deadline-aware prioritisation governs SC2 SCV pre-timing repair and SRE pre-incident hardening.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: disaster recovery, preventive maintenance scheduling, SC2 SCV repair
raw.author: openra-bench

The damage picture is misleading: the pillbox is the most worn (20%) and the loudest wear indicator, but it is low value, not load-bearing, and sits away from the coming stress. The refinery, war factory, and construction yard are the load-bearing assets and they are the ones the strike targets. The intended decision is preventive-maintenance triage: service the load-bearing plant to spec BEFORE the known stress event and keep the repair organ on it through the event — not the component whose wear gauge is reddest. Repairing the loud low-value decoys first, or stalling, loses the critical plant when the strike lands.
summary.zh: 您继承了一个安静的生产基地，该基地的五座建筑都受到了不同程度的预先损坏，并且在预定的压力事件发生之前您有一个维护窗口。损坏图片具有误导性：碉堡是磨损最严重的（20%），也是最响亮的磨损指示器，但它的价值较低，不承重，并且远离即将到来的压力。炼油厂、军工厂、建筑工地是承重资产，也是打击目标。预期的决定是预防性维护分类：在已知应力事件发生之前按照规范对承重设备进行维修，并在整个事件期间保持维修机构在其上，而不是磨损量表最红的部件。首先修复响亮的低价值诱饵，或者拖延，当攻击落地时会失去关键的植物。

YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 1501 OR NOT (own ≥1 'proc' building(s))).

WIN WHEN: own ≥1 'proc' building(s) AND own ≥1 'weap' building(s) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND not before game tick 900 AND before game tick 1300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 1301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'proc' building(s))).
You have at most 20 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same damaged base and heavy strike, but the base spawns from a seed-chosen column — a memorised opening fails. Read the actual building cells, toggle repair on the refinery, war factory, and yard, keep it on through the strike. Within about 15 turns.

YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 1301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'proc' building(s))).

title: Sell and Recoup Cash — Divest Obsolete Assets to Fund a Critical Purchase

raw.realWorldMeaning: The mission has shifted to offence: the agent must field a War Factory and a batch of 3 medium tanks, but starting cash alone does not cover that purchase and there is no income source. The base carries an over-built static-defence cluster (extra pillboxes, a Tesla coil, a radar dome) that the new objective no longer needs. The only path to the war factory and the tanks inside the tick budget is to SELL the now-obsolete defences — recovering 50% of their build cost as liquid cash — and reinvest that capital into the critical purchase. Stalling, buying without selling (cash-gated), and divesting but never buying all lose; only sell-then-buy wins.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Reallocate sunk capital from a deprecated subsystem to fund a newly-critical capability under a hard budget. A fleet carries redundant hardware provisioned for a mission profile that no longer applies; the operating reserve alone cannot commission the capability the current objective demands, and no fresh funding is incoming. The right move is a deliberate divestment of the obsolete hardware — salvaging roughly half its capital in liquid form — and reinvesting it into the new priority before the budget window closes. Holding the dead assets strands the capital and forfeits the objective.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: capital reallocation, asset divestment, SC2 sell mechanic
raw.author: openra-bench

title: MCV Deploy and Build — Site Choice + Commit + Basic Base

raw.realWorldMeaning: Critical-infrastructure siting under a commit-on-deploy constraint: the operator chooses a site to maximise defensibility, deploys the mobile asset (irreversibly converting it to a fixed Construction Yard at a known offset from the MCV cell), and then races the basic build chain (power online before the dependent barracks) before the clock. The decision is the SEQUENCE: site → deploy → power plant → barracks, where each step gates the next (no construction yard ⇒ cannot build; no power plant ⇒ barracks never completes) and where the deadline discriminates "deploys then idles" from "deploys then builds".
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Deployable autonomous factory: a mobile platform navigates to a siting cell and anchors (becomes a stationary production base); once anchored, the site is FIXED — the operator must then bring power online and stand up the first dependent module before the mission deadline. The commit is irreversible (no undeploy in this pack); a poor site is locked in.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE BuildOrderTimings, MicroRTS site-choice sub-tasks, urban planning facility-location, critical-infrastructure siting under defensibility
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Critical-infrastructure siting under a commit-on-deploy constraint: the operator chooses a site to maximise defensibility, deploys the mobile asset (irreversibly converting it to a fixed Construction Yard at a known offset from the MCV cell), and then races the basic build chain (power online before the dependent barracks) before the clock. The decision is the SEQUENCE: site → deploy → power plant → barracks, where each step gates the next (no construction yard ⇒ cannot build; no power plant ⇒ barracks never completes) and where the deadline discriminates "deploys then idles" from "deploys then builds".
summary.zh: 在部署时提交约束下的关键基础设施选址：运营商选择一个站点以最大化防御性，部署移动资产（不可逆地将其转换为与 MCV 单元已知偏移的固定施工场），然后在时钟之​​前对基本构建链进行竞赛（在相关兵营之前在线供电）。决策是顺序：场地→部署→发电厂→营房，其中每一步都关乎下一个步骤（没有施工场地⇒无法建造；没有发电厂⇒营房永远不会完工），并且截止日期区分“部署然后闲置”和“部署然后建造”。

en:
Deploy your MCV — that consumes the vehicle and creates a construction yard one cell up-and-left. From the yard queue a power plant ($300) adjacent, then a barracks ($500) adjacent. Yard, power plant, barracks, within about 50 turns. Not deploying or stopping early loses on the clock.
WIN WHEN: own a 'fact' AND own a 'powr' AND own a 'tent' AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR not before game tick 2000 AND NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 55 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same deploy-then-power-then-barracks chain, but the clock tightens to about 28 turns and a light Soviet patrol lurks. Deploy promptly, queue the power plant and barracks adjacent to the new yard. Losing the MCV to the patrol before deploy loses the run.
WIN WHEN: own a 'fact' AND own a 'powr' AND own a 'tent' AND before game tick 2500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2501 OR not before game tick 800 AND NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 30 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same chain under pressure with the MCV spawning in the NW or SW by seed and a richer 4-building goal: deploy, power plant, barracks, AND one extra building (a second power plant fits). Within about 34 turns. Stopping at three buildings loses.
WIN WHEN: own a 'fact' AND own a 'powr' AND own a 'tent' AND own ≥4 buildings total AND before game tick 3000.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3001 OR not before game tick 800 AND NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 36 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.
zh:

title: Deploy on Defensible Ground — Read the Map's Terrain Protection

raw.realWorldMeaning: Resilience-first siting under a KNOWN threat axis, decided by READING THE MAP'S DEFENSIVE GEOMETRY. The arena is a chokepoint map: two open lobes joined by a single narrow corridor through a thick water wall. The MCV starts AT the chokepoint mouth and a rusher band is committed from the EAST. Two candidate deploy sites exist: a DEFENSIBLE site BEHIND THE CHOKEPOINT WALL (in the WEST lobe — the rushers must funnel through one 4-cell corridor to reach it) and an INDEFENSIBLE site IN THE OPEN EAST LOBE (closer to the action but on the rusher's side of the wall, with no terrain protection). Once the MCV deploys, the site is committed — the conyard cannot be re-located. The decision is to pay the travel cost through the corridor to the lobe BEHIND THE WALL so the freshly placed construction yard + power + barracks + the first defender survive long enough to satisfy the build chain; siting on the indefensible (terrain-unprotected) side gets the construction yard razed inside the deploy + bring-up window.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous facility placement under a known disaster-direction: a single relocatable mobile base must commit to one of two candidate sites with a wildfire / attack vector already advancing from a known compass. The DEFENSIBLE (terrain-protected — behind a natural barrier with a single bottleneck) site costs travel time but survives bring-up; the INDEFENSIBLE (no natural cover) site is razed before the facility comes online. Mirrors FOB site selection and resilience-first siting in hazard-aware urban planning — the model must READ the map's defensive geometry, not pick the closest convenient cell.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: MicroRTS terrain-aware build, urban planning hazard-aware siting, military FOB site selection, resilience-first facility siting

summary.zh: 在已知的威胁轴下进行弹性优先的选址，通过阅读地图的防御几何结构来决定。竞技场是一张阻塞点地图：两个开放的波瓣由一条穿过厚厚的水墙的狭窄走廊连接起来。 MCV 从阻塞点口开始，并从东边派出冲锋队。存在两个候选部署地点：一个位于阻塞点墙后面的可防御地点（位于西瓣，冲锋者必须穿过一条 4 单元走廊才能到达），以及一个位于开放东瓣的不可防御地点（更靠近行动地点，但位于城墙的冲锋者一侧，没有地形保护）。一旦 MCV 部署完毕，场地即已确定——庭院无法重新定位。决定是支付穿过走廊到墙后面的波瓣的旅行费用，这样新放置的建筑场+电源+兵营+第一个防御者就能生存足够长的时间来满足建造链；选址在无法防御（不受地形保护）的一侧会导致部署+启动窗口内的施工场地被夷为平地。

Yard must land within radius 5 of (15,30). Deploying in the open EAST lobe fails the spatial check. Within about 54 turns.

YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4801 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) AND your whole force is destroyed OR not before game tick 1500 AND NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR not before game tick 2400 AND own a 'fact' AND NOT (have 1 building(s) near (15,30))).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: MCV Site Choice — Deploy Near the Ore Patch (Econ-First Siting)

raw.realWorldMeaning: Econ-first facility siting: a Construction Yard is most valuable when co-located with its raw-resource source. The starter MCV is the "movable" asset that pins the new base; the decision is WHERE to deploy. Deploying ADJACENT to the productive ore patch lands the new Yard inside the resource region (the win predicate gates exactly that). Deploying anywhere else — in place at the western starter base, mid-map, or on a decoy — leaves the construction yard predicate unsatisfied and the run runs out the clock as a LOSS.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous mining-base placement: the depot/processor must be placed near the ore body, not at an arbitrary staging point, or the collector's per-trip cost dominates throughput. Same idea in warehouse-near-rail, fab-near-silicon-source, distribution- centre-near-port siting (Weber facility-location problem).
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE econ optimization (worker travel minimization), MicroRTS resource-co-location, Weber facility-location problem, distribution-center / fab siting near supply source
raw.author: groupA-mcv-seed

summary.en: Econ-first facility siting: a Construction Yard is most valuable when co-located with its raw-resource source. The starter MCV is the "movable" asset that pins the new base; the decision is WHERE to deploy. Deploying ADJACENT to the productive ore patch lands the new Yard inside the resource region (the win predicate gates exactly that). Deploying anywhere else — in place at the western starter base, mid-map, or on a decoy — leaves the construction yard predicate unsatisfied and the run runs out the clock as a LOSS.
summary.zh: 经济优先的设施选址：当施工场地与其原材料来源位于同一地点时，其价值最高。启动 MCV 是固定新基地的“可移动”资产；决定是在哪里部署。将 ADJACENT 部署到生产矿区会将新 Yard 放置在资源区域内（获胜谓词正是如此）。在其他任何地方部署——在西部起始基地、地图中部或诱饵上——都会导致施工场谓词不满足，并且运行会导致损失。

en:
Drive the MCV east to the ore patch at (60,20) and deploy ADJACENT to it. Your starter base has a refinery and harvester already running so cash flows without further intervention; the only decision is the MCV deploy site. The win gates on a yard inside the ore-patch region AND cash 3000, within about 60 turns. Deploying in place leaves the yard far from the ore and misses the spatial gate. Stalling never builds the yard at all.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (60,20) AND reach economy value ≥3000 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401).
You have at most 62 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Drive the MCV east to the ore patch at (60,20) and deploy ADJACENT to it. Your starter base has a refinery and harvester already running at the western base so cash flows without further intervention. A single decoy ore patch (`mine`) sits halfway at (40,20) as a tempting near-mid site; ignore it — the win predicate gates on the real patch at (60,20). Win = yard in the ore-patch region AND cash 4000, within about 50 turns.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (60,20) AND reach economy value ≥4000 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501).
You have at most 52 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Your starter base spawns either NORTH (y=12) or SOUTH (y=28) by seed; each spawn has its OWN ore patch (same x=60) and its own pre-placed refinery + harvester. A shared far decoy ore patch sits at (88,20) but has no harvester positioned for it. Read your MCV's row, drive it east, and deploy adjacent to YOUR local ore patch — a memorised deploy cell fails on the flip. Win = yard in YOUR near-patch region AND cash 5500, within about 60 turns.

title: Relocate Under Fire — Deploy a Fresh MCV at a Safe Site

raw.realWorldMeaning: Spin up a relocated site under attack: the active site (the pre-placed western Construction Yard) is taking damage from a committed rusher coming down the central lane, and the agent has a single FRESH MCV parked mid-map. The decision: where to deploy the new Construction Yard so operations continue if the original falls. Deploying the MCV in-place (still in the rusher's lane) just gives the attacker a second construction yard to raze; deploying at a SAFE relocation region (NE or SE corner, off the attack lane) keeps a Construction Yard alive past the original's loss. The original may or may not survive — that is accepted; the goal is to keep operating from SOME Construction Yard at episode end.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Deploy a backup base when the primary is compromised: the active waypoint is being overrun and a mobile carrier must redeploy at a safe location BEFORE (or just after) the primary is lost, so the operator keeps a live anchor to act from. Choosing a redeployment site still inside the attacker's footprint is a naive solution — the right move puts the new anchor outside the blast radius.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning under exogenous loss, ScienceWorld error recovery, MicroRTS rebuild-after-loss, business continuity / disaster recovery relocation
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Second-Base Ramp-Up — Deploy the 2nd MCV at the Target Region

raw.realWorldMeaning: Multi-site facility ramp-up — the second production site is not just a duplicate; it must be PLACED at the right location (the briefed expansion region) to add real capacity / redundancy. Deploying the spare MCV next to base #1, or in an unrelated corner, gives the headline "two facilities online" but ZERO geographic ramp-up. The good site has its own ore patch and unlocks a second economy + a second production queue (the parallel-production fix means a 2nd factory at the good site genuinely doubles throughput). The bad site duplicates the primary's coverage and adds nothing.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous fleet establishing a second forward operating base at a strategic location: the spare base-builder unit has to drive to the designated expansion zone — a flank with its own resource patch — and stand up the new FOB there, not just park next to FOB #1 or end up in the wrong sector. The new FOB unlocks a second production line (parallel-production: 2 factories = 2× build throughput) AND a second supply channel (its own patch); a duplicate-coverage FOB next to FOB #1 unlocks neither.

raw.author: openra-bench

title: MCV Deploy Third Base — Tri-Region Operational Footprint

raw.realWorldMeaning: Tri-region facility footprint — each site at the RIGHT region for coverage. The operator commits THREE indivisible mobile assets to three DISTINCT geographies so the resulting network covers all three regions. Bunching two assets in one region wastes a deploy and leaves one region uncovered; abandoning an asset entirely leaves another uncovered. The decision is committing each asset to its designated region (which the start positions hint at on easy and which the model must reason about on medium/hard).
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous-fleet multi-FOB deployment for redundant coverage — three mobile platforms each transition from mobile to fixed (deploy is irreversible: the platform anchors and converts into a forward operating base), one per designated coverage region, so the resulting tri-FOB network maximises overall coverage and redundancy across the operational theatre.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE 3-base macro, MicroRTS multi-front expansion, distribution-network multi-warehouse planning, tri-region operational footprint
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Tri-region facility footprint — each site at the RIGHT region for coverage. The operator commits THREE indivisible mobile assets to three DISTINCT geographies so the resulting network covers all three regions. Bunching two assets in one region wastes a deploy and leaves one region uncovered; abandoning an asset entirely leaves another uncovered. The decision is committing each asset to its designated region (which the start positions hint at on easy and which the model must reason about on medium/hard).
summary.zh: 三区域设施足迹 - 每个站点位于正确的区域以进​​行覆盖。该运营商将三个不可分割的移动资产分配给三个不同的地区，因此最终的网络覆盖所有三个地区。将两项资产捆绑在一个区域会浪费部署并使一个区域未被覆盖；完全放弃一项资产会导致另一项资产未被覆盖。该决定是将每个资产提交到其指定的区域（在简单的情况下起始位置暗示该区域，在中/困难的情况下模型必须对其进行推理）。

WIN WHEN: own ≥3 'fact' building(s) AND have 1 building(s) near (130,15) AND have 1 building(s) near (130,65) AND have 1 building(s) near (75,70) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR not before game tick 4500 AND NOT (own ≥2 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 75 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

WIN WHEN: own ≥3 'fact' building(s) AND have 1 building(s) near (130,15) AND have 1 building(s) near (130,65) AND have 1 building(s) near (75,70) AND before game tick 6300.

title: Secure-Expand — Defend Base #1 While Base #2 Stands Up

raw.realWorldMeaning: Multi-front operations under disruption: a live production site is being probed while a second site has to come online elsewhere. The decision is not "defend OR expand" but "do BOTH IN PARALLEL" — keep the live site's key building alive (engage the probe with the on-site defenders) AND get the spare base-builder to the briefed expansion region and stand the new site up there. A single-track policy (only defend / only expand) loses either the base or the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Operations continuity during a fleet expansion: an autonomous site is under low-grade attack while a mobile platform is en route to anchor a second forward base at a designated region. Two crews working in parallel — site security on the live FOB, transit-and-anchor on the new one — beats either crew solo.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 secure-expand timing, MicroRTS expand-vs-defend tradeoff, BCP capacity ramp during operational disruption, site-B build while site-A operational

title: Mirror Base — East/West Geographic Redundancy Under Coordinated Attack

raw.realWorldMeaning: Geographic mirror redundancy under simultaneous pressure. You hold a fully built primary base in the WEST (construction yard + ore refinery + power plant + tank defenders on HOLD-FIRE) and a HALF-built standby in the EAST (just the construction yard). A coordinated probe pressures BOTH bases simultaneously. You must (a) defend the WEST primary — your HoldFire tanks will NOT engage on their own; only an explicit attack order makes them fight, (b) defend the EAST standby — same constraint with its own tank group, and (c) MIRROR the standby to functional parity with the primary by building a power plant AND a Refinery (ore refinery) at the east. Defending only one base loses the other replica; pausing the standby buildout to fight loses the SLA window on the mirror; ignoring defence to focus on the buildout loses both facts to the rush. Only a play that streams BOTH defence operations AND the east buildout from turn 1 keeps both replicas alive before the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Distributed-systems mirror / raft replicas / multi-region cloud failover under simultaneous incident pressure. Two geographic replicas must remain in functional parity; an incident that takes out EITHER replica breaks quorum. Standing up the standby region to parity (capacity-add) WHILE both regions are under attack requires parallel work streams — the on-call cannot serialize (handle the primary incident, then the secondary, then provision the standby capacity) without busting the cross-region SLA window.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: distributed-systems mirror, raft-style replicas, multi-region cloud
raw.author: openra-bench

You hold a fully built primary base in the WEST (construction yard + ore refinery + power plant + tank defenders on HOLD-FIRE) and a HALF-built standby in the EAST (just the construction yard). You must (a) defend the WEST primary — your HoldFire tanks will NOT engage on their own; only an explicit attack order makes them fight, (b) defend the EAST standby — same constraint with its own tank group, and (c) MIRROR the standby to functional parity with the primary by building a power plant AND a Refinery (ore refinery) at the east. Defending only one base loses the other replica; pausing the standby buildout to fight loses the SLA window on the mirror; ignoring defence to focus on the buildout loses both facts to the rush. Only a play that streams BOTH defence operations AND the east buildout from turn 1 keeps both replicas alive before the deadline.
summary.zh: 同时压力下的地理镜像冗余。你在西部拥有一个完全建成的主要基地（建筑场+矿石精炼厂+发电厂+保持火力状态的坦克防御者），在东部拥有一个半建成的备用基地（只是建筑场）。协调的探针同时对两个碱基施加压力。你必须 (a) 保卫西部初选——你的 HoldFire 坦克不会自行交战；只有明确的攻击命令才会让他们战斗，（b）保卫东部备用部队——与自己的坦克群同样受到限制，以及（c）通过在东部建造一座发电厂和一座精炼厂，使备用部队与主要部队的功能对等。只保卫一个基地就会失去另一个基地；暂停备用扩展以进行战斗会丢失镜像上的 SLA 窗口；忽视防守而专注于扩建，就会因为匆忙而失去这两个事实。只有从第一回合开始同时传输防御行动和东部建设的戏剧才能在截止日期之前保持两个副本的活力。

title: Redundant Production — Build a Backup War Factory (N+1 Planning)

raw.realWorldMeaning: Production resilience through N+1 redundancy. The agent inherits a working base whose only unit-producing structure — a single War Factory — is a known single point of failure: it is exposed and WILL be destroyed by an enemy strike in the opening. The capacity-planning task is to provision a SECOND War Factory in a safe location BEFORE the exposed one falls, so unit production survives the loss. A policy that runs the single factory until it dies halts production permanently and never fields its army; a policy that pre-builds the redundant factory keeps producing and meets the bar. This is robust capacity planning: never operate a critical capability on a single point of failure — stand up the backup ahead of the foreseen failure, not after it.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: N+1 redundancy for a critical production node. An autonomous operation depends on a single assembly cell that sits in a hazard zone and is certain to be lost. Resilient planning commissions a redundant assembly cell in a protected location BEFORE the exposed one fails, so throughput continues uninterrupted. Waiting for the failure and then improvising a replacement blows the delivery deadline; provisioning the standby in advance — paying the redundancy cost up front — keeps the line running.

title: Rotating Production Pressure — Load-Balance Two Bases Under Alternating Raids

raw.realWorldMeaning: The agent runs two production bases. An enemy raids them on an alternating schedule — one base now, the other later. The agent cannot fight directly; its only defence is the tanks it builds, and produced units appear at whichever war factory is currently the primary one. The intended policy ROTATES production: it funnels the first batch of tanks to the base that is about to be raided, then rotates the primary war factory so the next batch garrisons the second base before ITS raid lands. Building the whole army at a single base leaves the other base undefended — its war factory and Construction Yard are razed. The agent must read the alternating-pressure pattern and re-route production to the currently-threatened base.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Load-balancing a fleet of production cells under a moving fault: a logistics network has two depots and a disruption that migrates between them. Routing every replenishment run to one depot starves the other exactly when the disruption hits it. The controller must track which site is currently under stress and dynamically re-route capacity to the at-risk site BEFORE the disruption arrives — anticipatory load balancing, not reactive catch-up.

raw.author: openra-bench

title: Supply-Line Link — Patrol the Corridor Between Two Bases

raw.realWorldMeaning: Two bases are joined by a single overland supply corridor; raider bands probe into that corridor from the flanks. The agent commands a mobile squad of four tanks and must POSITION them ON the corridor — at its midpoint, not parked at either base — so that every raider band is interdicted mid-route before it can peel off and raze a base building. Garrisoning a single base over-defends it while leaving the far base and the corridor open; splitting the squad 2/2 across the two bases leaves the corridor itself undefended and the central bands slip through. Only a squad positioned along the link interdicts every band. This is the decision drill of supply-line protection: the threat is to the LINK, and the defensive capacity belongs on the corridor, not on the endpoints.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Logistics route security: a convoy lane connecting two depots must be patrolled along its length. Posting all security at the depots (the nodes) leaves the route (the edge) open to interdiction — the canonical convoy-ambush failure mode. A mobile patrol shadowing the lane intercepts threats in transit; static gate guards at each depot do not. Same total security capacity, different topology, qualitatively different route survivability.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: military supply-line protection, logistics route security, SC2 harass-route defense
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Two-Base Role Specialization — Tech Site vs Economy Site

raw.realWorldMeaning: Role specialization across two physical sites. The agent has two disjoint base footprints and an indivisible budget for the next couple of structures; one site must take the TECH role (war factory / R&D campus) and the other the ECONOMY role (refinery / production campus / storage). Bunching both roles at one site yields the headline "two production lines online" but fails the geographic specialization the brief demands. The SE pole sits next to the larger ore patch — ECONOMY-at-SE / TECH-at-NW is the rational assignment; the reverse is logistically possible but sub-optimal.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-warehouse role optimization: a logistics network with two facility footprints decides which one becomes the consolidation/ throughput hub (close to the inbound source) and which becomes the value-add / specialized assembly site (further from supply, nearer the shipping edge). Misallocating roles forces wasteful cross-site transfers and blows the SLA clock.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: industrial specialization (R&D campus vs production campus), SC2 specialized-base placements (tech base vs macro base), OR multi-warehouse role optimization, distributed-systems read-replica vs write-primary
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Role specialization across two physical sites. The agent has two disjoint base footprints and an indivisible budget for the next couple of structures; one site must take the TECH role (war factory / R&D campus) and the other the ECONOMY role (refinery / production campus / storage). Bunching both roles at one site yields the headline "two production lines online" but fails the geographic specialization the brief demands. The SE pole sits next to the larger ore patch — ECONOMY-at-SE / TECH-at-NW is the rational assignment; the reverse is logistically possible but sub-optimal.
summary.zh: 跨两个物理站点的角色专业化。代理有两个不相交的基地足迹和接下来几个结构的不可分割的预算；一个站点必须承担技术角色（战争工厂/研发园区），另一个站点必须承担经济角色（炼油厂/生产园区/存储）。将这两种角色集中在一个站点会产生“两条在线生产线”的标题，但未能满足简要要求的地理专业化。东南极位于较大的矿区旁边——东南经济/西北科技是合理的分配；相反的情况在逻辑上是可能的，但不是最优的。

en:
Two base sites: a NW pole at (20,20) and a SE pole at (140,60), each with a yard, power plant, and idle MCV. One harvester parked at NW. A large ore patch sits beside SE — that's the economy site; the shielded NW pole is the tech site. Cash $4000. Build the war factory at NW and the refinery at SE; two harvesters, economy value 2500, within about 70 turns.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (20,20) AND have 1 building(s) near (140,60) AND have ≥2 'harv' AND reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR NOT (own ≥2 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same NW and SE poles. The economy bar requires real harvest income — only the SE refinery can clear it inside the clock, because the free harvester it spawns hits the big patch immediately. War factory at NW, refinery at SE. Two harvs, economy value 2500, within about 70 turns. Bunching both buildings at one pole fails the cross-region clause.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (20,20) AND have 1 building(s) near (140,60) AND have ≥2 'harv' AND reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR NOT (own ≥2 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same role-split decision (war factory at NW, refinery at SE), but the starter harvester may spawn at the NW or SE pole by seed. The large patch is still by SE, so refinery-at-SE remains right either way. Read your actual layout. Two harvs, economy value 2500, within about 60 turns.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (20,20) AND have 1 building(s) near (140,60) AND have ≥2 'harv' AND reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥2 'fact' building(s))).

胜利条件：(20,20) 附近有 1 座建筑物，并且 (140,60) 附近有 1 座建筑物，并且拥有 ≥2 个“harv”，并且经济价值达到 ≥2500（现金+矿石），并且在游戏刻 6300 之前。
失败条件：（不在游戏前勾选 6301 或不（拥有 ≥2 个“事实”建筑物））。
您最多有 70 个决策回合；行动果断，尽早行动。

西北和东南极相同。经济条需要真正的收获收入——只有东南炼油厂才能在时钟内清除它，因为它产生的免费收割机会立即达到大块。西北为军工厂，东南为炼油厂。两次收获，经济值2500，大约70回合内。将两座建筑物集中在一根柱子上不符合跨区域条款。

title: Third Base Against the Clock — Greedy 3-Base Macro Expansion

raw.realWorldMeaning: A 3-base macro timing decision. The agent already runs two bases and a workable income; the next decision is whether to invest the incoming cash into ARMY (defence / pressure) or into a THIRD base site that secures long-term economic supremacy. The pack is tuned so that the agent CAN fund the 3rd refinery and stand the site up at the far-east target before the deadline IF they prioritise expansion — but the deadline is tight enough that a "spend on army instead" play forfeits the third base (the cash is gone, the new site never appears, the SLA expires) and a stall play (no decisions at all) likewise loses on the clock.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Industrial site expansion against an incumbent: a logistics operator with two live sites must stand a third site up by a contractual deadline to win the regional bid. Diverting capex into operational headcount at the existing sites (more drivers, more pickers) feels safer but blows the deadline; only committing the budget to the new site's groundworks delivers the third footprint in time.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 3-base macro, MicroRTS expansion, industrial site expansion

title: Multi-Front Build — Two Bases, Concurrent Refinery Ramp

raw.realWorldMeaning: Concurrent multi-site facility ramp under a shared bottleneck. The operator runs ONE central production queue but has TWO physically distant sites that each need a fresh production line online before the deadline. The decision is NOT "which site first" (both are required) but "keep the bottleneck queue saturated and pipeline placement at each site as the previous item completes". An operator who serializes (finish all work at site A before touching site B, inserting idle audit cycles between commands) blows the SLA on site B even when site A is flawless. The capability under test is split-attention pipelining: issuing the next start-of-build order on the very same turn the prior item lands at its target site.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Two greenfield robotics cells must each receive a critical fixture (refinery / palletizer) before the launch window. The fixture fabrication shop is shared (one fixture at a time), so the bottleneck is queue saturation, not transport. A scheduler that pipelines (fixture-1 build → install at cell A while fixture-2 already started) ships both cells in one launch window; a scheduler that batches (finish all of cell A, then start cell B from scratch) misses cell B's deadline despite identical total work.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 simultaneous-base macro, multi-plant manufacturing, distributed-systems geo-redundancy, multi-site facility ramp under a shared bottleneck
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Concurrent multi-site facility ramp under a shared bottleneck. The operator runs ONE central production queue but has TWO physically distant sites that each need a fresh production line online before the deadline. The decision is NOT "which site first" (both are required) but "keep the bottleneck queue saturated and pipeline placement at each site as the previous item completes". An operator who serializes (finish all work at site A before touching site B, inserting idle audit cycles between commands) blows the SLA on site B even when site A is flawless. The capability under test is split-attention pipelining: issuing the next start-of-build order on the very same turn the prior item lands at its target site.
summary.zh: 共享瓶颈下的并发多站点设施提升。该运营商运行一个中央生产队列，但有两个物理上相距较远的站点，每个站点都需要在截止日期之前上线一条新的生产线。决定不是“首先选择哪个站点”（两者都是必需的），而是“在前一个项目完成时保持瓶颈队列饱和并在每个站点放置管道”。即使站点 A 完美无缺，序列化的操作员（在接触站点 B 之前完成站点 A 上的所有工作，在命令之间插入空闲审核周期）也会破坏站点 B 上的 SLA。正在测试的功能是分散注意力管道：在前一个项目到达其目标站点的同一回合发出下一个开始构建命令。
